 Trending VIP How an ultra-early evaluation and long-term relationships helped Miami land elite WR Brysen Wright 
 Elite WR Brysen Wright commits to Miami, reclassifies to 2027
 Miami adds an elite wide receiver to its 2027 recruiting class after a major reclassification, giving the Hurricanes another star in their exceptional incoming class.
 Zach Blostein 33 Jacksonville (Fla.) Mandarin wide receiver Brysen Wright has committed to Miami and announced that he will reclassify from the 2028 class to the 2027 recruiting cycle .
 Wright, who ranked as the class of 2028's No. 10 overall prospect and No. 3 wide receiver , is a massive recruiting get for Miami, which will also get him to campus a year earlier than expected.
 Now in the 2027 class, 247Sports slots Wright as the No. 33 overall prospect.
 The 6-foot-3 1/2, 215-pound pass catcher chose Miami over programs like Florida ,  Ohio State  and  Texas .
 The Hurricanes have made Wright a top priority throughout his recruitment, which began when he was in middle school. The 'Canes were the first school to offer Wright a scholarship, which still holds weight, and he has since taken more trips to Coral Gables, Florida, than any other program.
 "Miami is on me the hardest," Wright said earlier this year. "They were the first school to offer me, so they have been on me hard for a long time. They have never let up. Miami is pushing for me hard and I like what they are doing."
 He also has multiple connections inside Miami's program.
 "I got a lot of relationships with players at Miami right now," Wright said. "(Wide receiver)  Somourian Wingo , I grew up with him. Malachi (Toney), I know him. A lot of them I know on that team. I can't even name them all, but I know a lot of them."
 His most recent trip to Miami sealed the deal for the Hurricanes.
 He took in Miami's Oct. 17 rivalry matchup with Florida State , which the 'Canes won in a double-overtime classic, and watched Toney turn in an exceptional performance. Wright then spent time on Miami's campus that Sunday, meeting with multiple members of the coaching staff, namely coach Mario Cristobal .
 Sources told 247Sports that Wright gave Miami his commitment at some point that day.
 With Wright now in the fold , Miami's 2027 class features commitments from multiple superstar talents. Aside from Wright, the 'Canes have five five-star prospects committed: cornerback Donte Wright , quarterback Israel Abrams , athlete A'mir Sears , wide receiver Nick Lennear and edge rusher Jaiden Bryant .
 247Sports director of scouting Andrew Ivins compares Wright to Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Drake London .
 – Big aerial specialist with plenty of viral moments to his name.
 – Believed to be north of 6-foot-3 and hovering somewhere around 210 pounds.
 – Can manufacture space like few others in recent cycles and turn 50-50 passes into 80-20 propositions with his bounce, coordination and extension.
 – Uses power to meet throws in traffic and by the sideline.
 – Quick to capitalize on RAC opportunities with his vision and momentum.
 – Consistently creates opportunities for his quarterback at all three levels but can be more of a one-speed route runner who lacks ideal separation quickness.
 – Showcases desired physicality on defense while doubling as a safety and can bring it as a perimeter blocker when engaged.
 – Must buy into the process but projects as a high-volume target on Saturdays who can be positioned around formations while hunting matchups.
